title: Brainstorm
description: The conversation held with the author of a request before any code is written, and what the factory understood from it. An input to the spec stage, never a document the person reviews. Doc 09.

understood.description: What the factory believes is being asked, in its own words, played back and left uncorrected. When this can be written without filling anything in, the conversation is over. That is the end condition; there is no turn limit.

open.description: Questions still outstanding. Empty is what 'enough' looks like.

holder.description: The run holding this conversation open. With heartbeat_at it answers the one question intake has to get right: is somebody already listening? Absent means nobody is.

heartbeat_at.description: When the holder last said it was still waiting, refreshed on every poll. A fresh one means a job will pick the next comment up itself, so intake must not start a second conversation and ask the person the same thing twice. A stale one means that job is gone.

last_comment_id.description: The last issue comment this conversation has accounted for, so a holder knows what is new and a restarted one does not answer the same thing twice.

frame.description: The expert words for what is being asked, worked out early in the conversation and taught to the person. A request filed in vague words gets built in vague words, and the one thing that changes that is naming it — but the naming has to reach the person, not just the factory, or every later question lands on somebody who has no word for the thing being asked about and the answers are guesses. Posted as a turn, never as a gate: they engage with the vocabulary or they just answer the question at the end of it. Also read by the spec stage, which has the research egress the conversation does not and so is the only stage that can confirm any of it; everything here is the conversation's unverified claim.

readings.description: When the request could name more than one problem, the problems it could be. Asking which, with the sign that tells them apart, is a better first question than any open one, because it is a question only the person can answer and the answer changes everything downstream.

problem.description: The problem this reading says they have, in a plain sentence.

term.description: The one term that names that problem.

tells_it_apart.description: The sign that distinguishes this reading from the others. The thing to actually ask about.

reading_taken.description: Which reading the conversation proceeded on, and why. Recorded even when the person chose it, because the spec stage inherits the choice and should know it was one.

named.description: What this is, in one plain sentence with the one term that names it. The spine of the frame turn, and the thing repeated in the playback at the end.

terms.description: The expert words, ranked by how much each would change what gets built — not alphabetically and not by how clever they sound. The top few are taught to the person; the rest are for the spec stage. Unverified: see this object's own description.

means.description: What it means, in one plain sentence. Not a definition copied from somewhere.

names.description: The part of what they actually said that this word names. A term that names nothing they said is a term the conversation went looking for.

prior_art.description: A real project, paper or system that uses the term this way, named rather than linked. Unverified, like everything here.

unlocks.description: What having this word lets someone ask for that they could not ask for before. A term that unlocks nothing is vocabulary for its own sake; leave it out.

neighbors.description: Fields that solved this shape of problem under other names. The point is the research anchor: a spec stage told 'this is a work-stealing queue, the neighbours are OS schedulers and print spoolers' searches for something, where one told nothing searches for the issue title.

carries_over.description: What transfers from that field to this problem.

breaks_down.description: Where the analogy fails. Required, because an analogy with no stated limit is the one that gets over-applied.

terms.description: Terms that come back from that field.

unmentioned.description: What they did not mention and should care about. Each one is either asked as a turn or carried here for the spec stage; it is never silently dropped.
